issue_context.title: CFB8 mode with zero padding produces exception when encrypting
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @bartonjs, @vcsjones, @krwq, @jeffhandley See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description The following code will produce an exception inside of `UniversalCryptoEncryptor`: ```c# using System.Security.Cryptography; using Aes aes = Aes.Create(); aes.Mode = CipherMode.CFB; aes.FeedbackSize = 8; aes.Padding = PaddingMode.Zeros; using var transform = aes.CreateEncryptor(); byte[] data = new byte[7]; byte[] result = transform.TransformFinalBlock(data, 0, data.Length); ``` results in: ``` Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentException: Destination is too short. (Parameter 'destination') at Internal.Cryptography.UniversalCryptoEncryptor.PadBlock(ReadOnlySpan`1 block, Span`1 destination) at Internal.Cryptography.UniversalCryptoEncryptor.UncheckedTransformFinalBlock(ReadOnlySpan`1 inputBuffer, Span`1 outputBuffer) at Internal.Cryptography.UniversalCryptoEncryptor.UncheckedTransformFinalBlock(Byte[] inputBuffer, Int32 inputOffset, Int32 inputCount) at Internal.Cryptography.UniversalCryptoTransform.TransformFinalBlock(Byte[] inputBuffer, Int32 inputOffset, Int32 inputCount) ``` Doesn't seem that the size of `data` matters, it will always produce an exception. ### Configuration .NET 5, Linux. ### Regression? The mode is new in .NET 5, however is a regression from .NET Framework.
Author: vcsjones
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Security`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

This looks suspect. This was not updated to account for alignment other than the block size. Will fix and add tests.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5b48caed15190568f3573cc9a1f96bfec357b485/src/libraries/Common/src/Internal/Cryptography/UniversalCryptoEncryptor.cs#L159-L164

review_comments: Since `Zero` padding does nothing when the input is aligned correctly, and for CFB8 means "any length is aligned correctly", there is no meaningful difference between `None` and `Zeros` when using CFB8, so we can re-use that existing tests.
